newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain, Italy reaffirm aim to be part of EMU launch.
newsitem.headline: Spain, Italy reaffirm aim to be part of EMU launch.

text.p: Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar and Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi confirmed on Tuesday their will to take part in the launch of Europe's single currency in 1999.
"Spain will do whatever is necessary to enter in the first group of countries of European Monetary Union," Aznar said at a joint press conference.

"Spain has decided to participate in monetary union from the beginning" Aznar said. "The (Spanish) government will reach and maintain, as I am doing, all the measures needed so that Spain could start in the leading countries."
"Both countries want to be part of the European Union," Prodi said. "We do not think that the future of either country has any alternative but to start with Europe."
When asked if Italy's commitment was as staunch as Spain's, Prodi said "(Our) intention has the same solidity. Both confirm our intention to be part of the single currency from the beginning".
Prodi and Aznar were holding a joint press conference after a bilateral summit in Valencia.

Both agreed that unemployment was one of the most important issues facing the two nations. Prodi said that even though this remains a domestic problem, European guidelines might offer some help. He gave no specifics.
